Lessons.Title: Build Fractions from Unit Fractions
ExplanationParagraphs: 2021 warm-up Number Talk: 3 × 3 = 9, 7 × 3 = 21, 10 × 3 = 30, 3 × 17 = 51. The last product can be decomposed as 3 × (10 + 7) = 30 + 21 = 51. These multiplication expressions support repeated-unit counting; they are not equivalent to partitioning unequal regions.

Activity 1, Introduce Secret Fractions: use separate facedown secret-fraction and unit-fraction decks. Each player draws two target (secret) fractions. On a turn, choose one unit-fraction card OR exchange both target fractions for two new ones. Once a target can be assembled from collected unit-fraction pieces of the SAME unit whole and denominator, shade an independently drawn gameboard with equal-area parts to represent that target, then draw a replacement target. First player to build two targets wins. This is an open game with no fixed secret-fraction answers.

The unit-fraction rule is mathematical: copies of 1/n of the same whole build k/n. Thus four pieces of 1/8 make 4/8 (also 1/2), two pieces of 1/3 make 2/3, three pieces of 1/4 make 3/4, five pieces of 1/6 make 5/6. Do not add denominators when assembling equal-sized unit fractions, and do not combine differently sized wholes.

Activity 2, Represent Fraction Situations: Pilolo hiding places along a street. Draw four fresh and equally spaced 0-to-1 street-length strips representing 4/8 for a rock, 2/3 for a penny, 3/4 for a stick, and 5/6 for a penny. On each, the whole street length stays constant; make 8, 3, 4, or 6 equal divisions, respectively, and mark the corresponding distance from the starting point. These strips are new Edulytics mathematical diagrams, not publisher artwork.

Original activity also asks students to approximate the fraction for a marked stick in a separate source diagram. The answer cannot be fixed without inspecting the exact 2021 graphic; teacher reviews placement, unit length, estimation and mathematical explanation. Students' Pilolo contextual interpretation and gameboard shading are teacher-reviewed, not certified merely from a numeric answer.

Source review scope: three public student-facing HTML sections, six teacher headings and twelve alt-text figure descriptions are indexed; original publisher student-task PDF, publisher gameboard pixels, photograph and diagram geometry have not been individually visually verified. No third-party images or gated publisher Cool-down are embedded. A first-party independent assessment remains separate from publisher assessment.

KeyConcepts.Title: Unit fraction copies
KeyConcepts.Definition: A unit fraction 1/n is one of n equal-size parts of one fixed whole.
KeyConcepts.Rule: k copies of 1/n build k/n when the whole is consistent.
KeyConcepts.Example: Five 1/6-length intervals give 5/6 of one street.

KeyConcepts.Title: Build a secret target
KeyConcepts.Definition: Collect equal-sized unit-fraction representations until their total matches a target fraction.
KeyConcepts.Rule: For a target k/n, k copies of 1/n build the target.
KeyConcepts.Example: Three one-fourth cards can show 3/4; check the gameboard.

KeyConcepts.Title: Fraction of a length
KeyConcepts.Definition: A fraction of a street measures distance from zero along one complete street-length unit.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Divide the same whole into n equal lengths and take k successive intervals.
KeyConcepts.Example: 4/8 is halfway along the length; 2/3 is two thirds of the full street.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equivalent descriptions
KeyConcepts.Definition: Two fractions may name the same position with different equal partitions.
KeyConcepts.Rule: 4/8 = 1/2, but the source task still requires eighths.
KeyConcepts.Example: Do not replace the task's eight-part model by a sole two-part drawing.

WorkedExamples.Title: Four warm-up products
WorkedExamples.Question: Compute 3×3, 7×3, 10×3 and 3×17 mentally.
WorkedExamples.Method: Count equal groups and decompose 17 as 10+7.

WorkedExamples.Title: Secret fraction assembled from copies
WorkedExamples.Question: Can three 1/4 unit cards form 3/4 of one equal-area whole?
WorkedExamples.Method: Add equal-sized fractional parts, not denominators.
Steps: Represent four congruent quarters of that whole.
WorkedExamples.Check: Each part is one fourth of the SAME whole.

WorkedExamples.Title: Pilolo rock
WorkedExamples.Question: A rock is hidden 4/8 of the street from the start.
WorkedExamples.Method: Represent eight equal length intervals, mark the fourth.
Steps: Mark endpoints 0 and 1 for one street.
Divide the street into 8 equal intervals.
Mark the fourth tick at 4/8, halfway along.
WorkedExamples.Check: The distance is also 1/2 of the whole; eighths must remain visible.

WorkedExamples.Title: Pilolo first penny
WorkedExamples.Question: A penny is hidden 2/3 of the street from the start.
WorkedExamples.Method: Split the same-length whole into three equal intervals.
WorkedExamples.Check: Position lies between half and the street's end.

WorkedExamples.Title: Pilolo stick
WorkedExamples.Question: A stick is hidden 3/4 of the street from the start.

WorkedExamples.Title: Pilolo second penny
WorkedExamples.Question: A penny is hidden 5/6 of the street from the start.
Steps: Partition into six equal length intervals.
WorkedExamples.Check: One sixth of the street remains.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assume the four Pilolo pictures all use the same count of unit divisions.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Repartition each new unit strip in equal pieces for the indicated denominator.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Count four eighths as 4/16 by adding denominators.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Denominator records the size of one unit, not number of collected cards.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Keep denominator eight; sum four copies of 1/8 to get 4/8.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Claim Secret Fractions is a fixed-answer card game.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Original source gives player draws and permitted moves; targets change with cards.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Teacher reviews independent selections, gameboard equal-area shading and rule-following.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assign a fixed fraction to the final diagram's stick using alt-text alone.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The figure's exact geometric position has not been visually inspected.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Require the original diagram or teacher-attested representation before assigning or grading.

SummaryPoints: Build k/n as k same-whole copies of 1/n; Secret Fractions has variable targets and two win conditions.
Pilolo four marked distances: rock 4/8, penny 2/3, stick 3/4, penny 5/6.
The separate source-diagram stick estimate is teacher-only until original image geometry is verified.
Original student PDF, publisher gameboard/photo figures and Stage D remain unverified; do not promote this lesson based on text extraction alone.
